chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: Meeting Jimmy Blanton in Chicago with Ellington, 1939
summary: Stewart met Blanton in Chicago in about 1939 while Slim and Slam were playing there; Crouch recalls Billy Taylor leaving the Ellington band because of Blanton.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now, when did you meet Jimmy Blanton? Do you remember when you met him?
About '39, yes. I met him in Chicago. Slim and I were playing in Chicago at that time, and that's when I met Jimmy Blanton with Duke Ellington.
How did he strike you when you first heard him?
He was great. He was a wonderful, wonderful bassist.
Was he playing by himself with the band or was Billy Taylor playing the bass too? When he first came in the band they had two bass players. I think it was Billy Taylor --
Yeah, I think it was Billy and Jimmy.
Were they both together when you heard the band or was --

Yeah, because -- because Taylor, I think Taylor stayed in the band about two weeks after Jimmy was there. Then he told Billington that he had to quit because (inaudible) he couldn't stay. He'd Blanton. He started to be embarrassed.
Well, anyway, I had the pleasure of meeting Jimmy when only he was with Duke. He was really a great bass -- bassist.
